# jubarte

[![CI](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/jubarte-redlines.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/jubarte-redlines)
[![docs.rs](https://docs.rs/jubarte-redlines/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/jubarte-redlines)
[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/jubarte-redlines.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/jubarte-redlines/)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/jubarte-wasm.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jubarte-wasm)
[![MSRV](https://img.shields.io/badge/MSRV-1.94-blue)](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/Cargo.toml)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0--only-blue.svg)](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/LICENSE)

**Word-faithful DOCX redlines and rendering, without Word.**

Compare two Word documents into native tracked changes, inspect or resolve
changes programmatically, apply validated edit plans, and render DOCX to PDF
or PNG — from Rust, Python, Node/browser, or the CLI.

Jubarte is an in-process DOCX engine for applications that need Microsoft
Word-style review workflows without automating Microsoft Word or LibreOffice.

- **Compare DOCX → tracked DOCX** with native insertions, deletions, moves and
  formatting changes.
- **List, accept or reject changes** globally or selectively by change ID,
  author and kind.
- **Render DOCX → PDF / PNG** with an independent Word-oriented layout engine.
- **Inspect and edit documents safely** using paragraph IDs, source hashes and
  atomic JSON edit plans.
- **Use the same core engine everywhere**: Rust, CLI, Python and WebAssembly
  for Node/browser.
- **Keep the original package**: relationships, styles, headers/footers,
  notes, media and other DOCX parts are preserved by the comparison workflow.

> Jubarte is not affiliated with Microsoft. “Word-faithful” describes
> engineering targets measured against Microsoft Word behavior; it is not a
> claim that every DOCX will render byte-for-byte or page-for-page identically.

**Live benchmark, every page against Microsoft Word:
[jandira-tech.github.io/neurotic_docx_bench](https://jandira-tech.github.io/neurotic_docx_bench/)**
· tables: [neurotic_docx_bench RESULTS.md](https://github.com/jandira-tech/neurotic_docx_bench/blob/main/RESULTS.md)

## Quick start

Install the CLI:

```sh
cargo install jubarte-redlines
jubarte --version
```

Prebuilt archives are also published on
[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/releases).
Check the assets attached to the release you intend to install.

### Compare two Word documents

```sh
jubarte original.docx modified.docx \
  -o redline.docx \
  --author "Reviewer"
```

`redline.docx` contains native Word tracked changes.

Without `-o`, jubarte prints the redline as the agent view and writes
nothing; `-o redline.pdf` renders it instead.

### Inspect and resolve tracked changes

```sh
jubarte changes redline.docx          # one change per line (a replacement is one): r12, kind, target, author, paragraph, text

# Resolve one specific change and leave the others tracked:
jubarte accept redline.docx \
  -o partially-accepted.docx \
  --id r12

# Or resolve everything:
jubarte accept redline.docx -o final.docx
jubarte reject redline.docx -o original-state.docx
```

Selection flags can be repeated and combined:

```sh
jubarte reject redline.docx \
  -o reviewed.docx \
  --author "Reviewer A" \
  --kind formatting
```

### Render DOCX to PDF or PNG

```sh
# PDF
jubarte convert redline.docx \
  -o redline.pdf \
  --revisions word \
  --compress

# Page images: redline-page-01.png, redline-page-02.png, ...
jubarte convert redline.docx \
  -o redline.png \
  --dpi 120
```

No Microsoft Word or LibreOffice process is launched.

## How the workflow fits together

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[original.docx] --> C[Compare]
    B[modified.docx] --> C
    C --> D[redline.docx]
    D --> E[List changes]
    E --> F[Accept / Reject]
    F --> G[resolved.docx]

    H[DOCX] --> I[Read]
    I --> J[JSON edit plan]
    J --> K[Edit]
    K --> L[clean.docx]
    K --> M[redline.docx]

    D --> N[Render]
    G --> N
    L --> N
    M --> N
    N --> O[PDF / PNG]
```

## Install

### CLI

```sh
cargo install jubarte-redlines
```

The installed binary is named `jubarte`.

From 0.11.0, the Python wheel and the npm package also run the CLI
without an install:

```sh
uvx jubarte-redlines redline a.docx b.docx -o redline.docx
npx jubarte-redlines redline a.docx b.docx -o redline.docx
```

Both runners speak the shared command set — `compare`/`redline`, `diff`,
`changes`, `accept`, `reject`, `read`, `edit`, `add`,
`convert`, `capabilities` — and share the Rust clap parser for help,
defaults, aliases and usage errors. The Python wheel also runs `comments`,
`validate` and `visual-diff`; `append`, `scrub`, `debug` and `self-update`
remain in the binary. The npm CLI renders no PNG pages
([`jubarte-wasm/cli/README.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/jubarte-wasm/cli/README.md)).

For a GitHub-style text review of two Word documents:

```sh
jubarte diff a.docx b.docx --format github
jubarte diff a.docx b.docx --format github --context 5 -o changes.patch
uvx jubarte-redlines diff a.docx b.docx --format github
npx jubarte-redlines diff a.docx b.docx --format github
```

`github` (also `unified` or `text`) prints a standard unified patch with
`diff --git`, file headers, hunk ranges and context. It compares the complete
`debug -c text` view, including existing revision marks and story text in
headers, footers, notes, comments, tables and text boxes. It extracts all content before display clipping and never caps the number of changes, and does not create an implicit
DOCX. Header/footer part renumbering is paired by section role. This is a
patch of extracted **text**, for review; it cannot patch a binary DOCX.
Formatting and media differences belong to `compare`, `debug` or `visual-diff`.

CriticMarkup keeps its existing role: representing a document's current
content with its tracked marks and comments. `github` gives a separate
comparison of those contents; it does not accept, reject or reinterpret the
marks unless `--accept-changes` is requested. `--format word` always accepts
ALL changes in both inputs first, then produces fresh word-level CriticMarkup.
`normal`, `context` and `side-by-side` are also available. Long lines show a
70-character window around the first change; `--full-lines` shows everything.
See [text diff details](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/TEXT_DIFF.md).

Markdown sits beside Word: `jubarte diff` prints the changes between any
two documents, Word or Markdown, as a git-style patch; `jubarte convert
draft.md` writes CommonMark (with CriticMarkup as tracked changes) to
DOCX/PDF/PNG; and `jubarte edit` writes the redline's patch as
`patch.diff`. See [`docs/MARKDOWN.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/MARKDOWN.md).

For a source checkout, the repository also contains installation scripts that
can install supplemental fonts used by the renderer:

```sh
scripts/install.sh
scripts/install.sh --fonts-only
```

On Windows, see `scripts/install.ps1`.

### Rust library

```sh
cargo add jubarte-redlines --no-default-features
```

The package is called `jubarte-redlines`; the Rust library import path is
`jubarte`.

```rust
use jubarte::{convert, document_comparer};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let original = std::fs::read("original.docx")?;
    let modified = std::fs::read("modified.docx")?;

    let redline =
        document_comparer::compare_documents(&original, &modified, "Reviewer")?;
    std::fs::write("redline.docx", &redline)?;

    let pdf = convert::docx_to_pdf(&redline)?;
    std::fs::write("redline.pdf", &pdf)?;

    Ok(())
}
```

The default crate features include the CLI, fast allocator and self-update
support. Library-only consumers can disable defaults and opt into features
deliberately.

MSRV: **Rust 1.94**.

### Python

Python requires CPython 3.10 or later.

```sh
pip install jubarte-redlines
```

Low-level byte API:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from jubarte_redlines import (
    compare_documents,
    get_revisions,
    docx_to_pdf,
)

original = Path("original.docx").read_bytes()
modified = Path("modified.docx").read_bytes()

redline = compare_documents(
    original,
    modified,
    author="Reviewer",
)
Path("redline.docx").write_bytes(redline)

for revision in get_revisions(redline):
    print(revision)

Path("redline.pdf").write_bytes(
    docx_to_pdf(redline, revisions="word")
)
```

The richer `Document` API additionally supports inspection, Markdown
projection, selective change resolution, edit plans, PDF/PNG rendering and
preview.

### Node and browser

Node 18+:

```sh
npm install jubarte-wasm
```

```js
const {
  compareDocuments,
  docxToPdf,
  listChanges,
  acceptChanges,
  rejectChanges,
} = require("jubarte-wasm");

const redline = compareDocuments(originalBytes, modifiedBytes, "Reviewer");
const pdf = docxToPdf(redline, false, "word");
```

For applications that do not need the PDF renderer, use the slim package
exports:

```js
const {
  compareDocuments
} = require("jubarte-wasm/slim");
```

Browser builds are exported from `jubarte-wasm/web` and
`jubarte-wasm/web-slim`.

### MCP server

`jubarte-mcp` exposes the engine as MCP tools (read, edit as tracked
changes, render, compare, accept and reject) to coding agents. Every path
stays under `--root`.

| Host | Install |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport stdio jubarte --scope project -- uvx --from 'jubarte-redlines[mcp]' jubarte-mcp --root .` |
| Codex | `codex mcp add jubarte -- uvx --from 'jubarte-redlines[mcp]' jubarte-mcp --root .` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini extensions install https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines` |

Tools, security model and config files: [docs/adoption/mcp.md](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/adoption/mcp.md).

## CLI reference

Every command, from `jubarte --help` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_docs.sh`).
The complete per-command `--help` of every runner (the `jubarte` binary, the
Python wheel, the npm CLI) is in the [per-surface guides](#documentation).

<!-- gen:cli-summary:start -->
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `jubarte ORIGINAL MODIFIED` | Read, edit, compare and render Word documents |
| `jubarte compare` | Compare documents: print the redline as the agent view, or write it with -o [alias: redline] |
| `jubarte changes` | List tracked changes with IDs for accept, reject and edit plans |
| `jubarte accept` | Accept all tracked changes, or select by ID, author or kind |
| `jubarte reject` | Reject all tracked changes, or select by ID, author or kind |
| `jubarte convert` | Convert Word or Markdown to DOCX, PDF, PNG or Markdown |
| `jubarte diff` | Review differences as GitHub, word, normal, context or side-by-side text |
| `jubarte read` | Read the agent view: YAML header, `<!-- pN -->` id lines, changes and comments with ids |
| `jubarte edit` | Edit a document: -p WHERE with --anchor, --content, --delete, --resolve, --reply, --accept, --reject, --strike, --restore or --style (several -p per command), or a JSON plan. Writes FILE_modified.docx (--in-place replaces FILE; --out-dir: the bundle), then prints SUCCESS and a fenced before/after diff of the full agent views (refusal: exit 3) |
| `jubarte add` | Add a paragraph, a comment or a reply: -p WHERE --content TEXT (several -p per command). Writes FILE_modified.docx, as edit does (--in-place replaces FILE), and prints SUCCESS and a fenced before/after diff of the full agent views |
| `jubarte capabilities` | What this binary can do, for agents choosing an operation |
| `jubarte visual-diff` | Compare rendered pages pixel by pixel (different pages: exit 5) |
| `jubarte comments` | List comments, threads and the text they annotate |
| `jubarte append` | Join documents in order, preserving images, styles, lists and notes |
| `jubarte validate` | Check Word validity, tracked edits, accessibility, style and structure; or repair Word validity |
| `jubarte check` | Check a document against a source-bound expectation contract |
| `jubarte scrub` | Remove authors, editing IDs, metadata and comments before sharing |
| `jubarte self-update` | Check or install a release from GitHub |
<!-- gen:cli-summary:end -->

### Compare

```text
jubarte ORIGINAL MODIFIED [OPTIONS]
```

Without `-o`, `jubarte A B` (or `jubarte compare A B`) prints the redline
as the agent view (the `read` options apply) and writes nothing. With `-o`,
the extension picks what is written:

| `-o` | Writes |
|---|---|
| `.docx` (or no or an unknown extension) | the redline |
| `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt` | the agent view of the redline; CriticMarkup when both inputs are Markdown |
| `.pdf` | the redline, rendered (`--revisions`, `--pages`, `--changed-pages` apply) |
| `.png` | one `STEM-page-NN.png` per page |
| `.json` | the snapshot of the redline, as `read --json` prints it |

`jubarte FILE` alone is `jubarte read FILE`; a lone name without an
extension is taken for a mistyped task, so read such a file with
`jubarte read FILE`.

Common options:

| Option | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-b, --original FILE` | Original document |
| `-m, --modified FILE` | Modified document |
| `-o, --output FILE` | Write the redline; the extension picks the format (above) |
| `-a, --author NAME` | Revision author (default: `Redline`) |
| `-d, --datetime ISO8601` | Revision timestamp (default: now, UTC) |
| `--detail-threshold RATIO` | Comparison-detail tuning |
| `--mode word|powertools` | Word-oriented or classic PowerTools comparison behavior |
| `--force` | Replace an existing output |
| `--reference-doc FILE`, `--critic`, `--resource-path DIR` | Markdown inputs |
| `--revisions`, `--dpi`, `--pages`, `--changed-pages` | Rendering, for `-o FILE.pdf` or `.png` |
| `-q, --quiet` | No status lines on success; a reading task still prints what it read |

The command line dates the revisions now; pin `-d 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` for
byte-identical output from identical inputs. The library calls keep the
epoch as their default, so they stay deterministic.

### List tracked changes

```sh
jubarte changes FILE.docx
jubarte changes FILE.docx --json
```

`changes` is intended for individually addressable review operations and
reports stable IDs while the corresponding tracked change remains present.
The text listing prints short ids (`r12`, `header1.r1`, `footnotes.r3`);
`--json` prints JSON Lines with the same short `id` (and `ref`). `--id`
takes the short ids: `r12`, `r1+2` (both marks of one
change), `header1.r1`. A change that holds a comment's reference mark ends
its line with `holds comment c4's mark` (`holds comment marks c4, c5` for a
thread's reply too), and `--json` lists them in `holds_comments`: resolving
the change so its content goes (accepting a deletion, rejecting an
insertion) removes those threads, as Word does. The `read` view says so on
the note: `{>>c4 @AC in r13: …<<}` when the note prints outside r13.


With human-readable CLI output, every command that writes a DOCX from a
document prints a confirmation after publication (unless `-q`):

````text
SUCCESS:
~~~~diff
--- before in.docx
+++ after out.docx
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 ---
-source: in.docx
+source: out.docx
 sha256: …
~~~~
````

The diff compares the full input and output agent views, including `source:`
and `sha256:`. It uses three context lines; the output view comes from the
published bytes. Markdown conversion uses the original Markdown text as its
before-view; comparison uses its first input. Identical views print
`no differences` inside the fence. The fence grows past any leading tilde
run in the diff. Edit's former changed-range view and resolved-lines output
are replaced by this block; an existing bundle summary stays before it,
with one block per DOCX. The `wrote …` lines and notes remain on stderr.
`-q` silences the block, summary and status; warnings and errors still print.
Dry runs, saved plans and non-DOCX outputs retain their existing output.
Template generation writes a JSON plan; applying it writes the DOCX.
Typed `--json`/`--jsonl` delivery retains its machine-readable receipt.

### Accept or reject

```sh
jubarte accept FILE.docx -o OUTPUT.docx
jubarte reject FILE.docx -o OUTPUT.docx
```

Optional selection filters:

```text
--id ID          r12, r1+2, header1.r1
--author NAME
--kind insertion|deletion|move|formatting
```

Filters are repeatable. Categories combine, so a change must satisfy each
category you supplied. `jubarte edit FILE -p r12 --accept` (or `--reject`)
resolves one change and writes `FILE_modified.docx`.

Add `--keep-nested-comment` to `accept` or `reject` to preserve a comment
and its replies when settlement removes their whole anchor. Their markers
move together to an empty, untracked anchor where the removed text was;
the command reports, for example, `kept c0 and its reply c1 on an empty anchor
in p1`. Partial overlaps keep the existing behavior. The default removes
wholly removed threads, as Word does.

### Convert to PDF / PNG

```sh
jubarte convert FILE.docx [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `-o, --output FILE` | Output path; the extension picks the format: `.docx`, `.md`, `.pdf`, `.png` (pages named `STEM-page-NN.png`) or `.json` (the snapshot) |
| `--dpi DPI` | PNG resolution; default 96 |
| `--compress` | Deflate PDF content streams |
| `--revisions conventional|word|custom` | Tracked-change visualization |
| `--keep-nested-comment` | With `--track-changes accept` or `reject`, keep comment threads whose whole anchor is removed, on an empty anchor; off by default |
| `--revision-palette SPEC` | Custom change colors/lines |
| `--font-report FILE` | Write font-resolution JSON |
| `--report FILE` | Write page/render report |
| `--force` | Replace existing output |
| `--fail-on-substitution` | Exit 4 when a requested font was substituted |
| `--pages SPEC` | Only these pages, for example `1-3,7`, in the PDF and the PNGs alike; PNGs keep the document's page numbers |
| `--move-comments` | List comments after the last page; the text keeps its tint and a `[JR1]` marker |
| `--changed-pages` | Keep only the pages a change touches: a body or note revision, a comment anchor, or the first page a revised header or footer paints on (page numbers stay the document's) |
| `-f, --from` / `-t, --to` | `docx`, `md`, `pdf`, `png` or `json`, when `-o` has no extension: Markdown in (CriticMarkup becomes tracked changes) or out ([`docs/MARKDOWN.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/MARKDOWN.md)) |

Without `-o`, a `.docx` becomes `STEM.pdf` beside it and Markdown becomes
`STEM.docx`; `-t md` prints to stdout.

Markdown to Word: a change or comment that names no author or date (by its
tag or the `authors:` table) takes `-a, --author` and `-d, --datetime`,
else the front matter's `author:` and `last_modified:` (else `modified:`,
`date:`, `created:`), else the `--reference-doc`'s `dc:creator` and
`dcterms:created`, else `Redline` and now. Pin `-d 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`
for byte-identical output; the library calls keep `Redline` and that
epoch as their default and read no reference document's metadata.
`compare`, `edit`, `add` and `diff` never take the files' metadata: their
changes carry `--author` and `--datetime` (default `Redline` and now).

Examples:

```sh
jubarte convert contract.docx
jubarte convert redline.docx --revisions word
jubarte convert redline.docx -o pages.png --dpi 144
jubarte convert long.docx -o excerpt.pdf --pages 1-3,7
jubarte convert redline.docx -o changed.pdf --changed-pages
jubarte convert contract.docx --compress --font-report fonts.json
```

A document with comments gets Word's markup pane: each comment in a
balloon beside its range, joined to it by a dotted connector, with the
range tinted and bracketed. As Word does, no style writes a PDF comment
annotation: a viewer would paint it as a note icon over the text
([`docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md)).

A custom palette can be supplied with:

```sh
jubarte convert redline.docx \
  --revisions custom \
  --revision-palette \
  "deleted=#AA0000:strike,inserted=#0055FF:double-underline"
```

### Read a document

```sh
jubarte read contract.docx               # the agent view
jubarte read contract.docx --json        # the snapshot: paragraphs, runs, tables, changes, comments
jubarte read contract.docx --tables      # top-level tN grids, with nested cell paths
jubarte read contract.docx --tables -p t0 # t0 and its nested tables: grid, then view
jubarte read contract.docx -p p12,p40-p48 -o excerpt.md
```

`read` prints the agent view: a YAML header (`sha256:` of the file, the
revision and comment counts, authors and their handles, page setup,
styles, headers, footers), then Markdown with an id line before every
paragraph (`p12`, the body's paragraph 12) and an id on every
tracked change and comment (`r3+4` is the two marks with `w:id` 3 and 4, `c5`
is comment 5, `header1.r1` a change in a header). A table cell's paragraph is
`t0.row1.cell2`, a footnote's `footnotes.p0`, and `c5.text` the text comment
5 covers. No id needs quoting in bash, zsh or csh.

`--json` prints the snapshot instead: document metadata, story and
paragraph coordinates, `source_sha256`, runs, structural limitations,
tables, content controls, and the changes and comments with their short
`ref`. The selection flags (`-p`, `--head`, `--tail`, `--changed`, `--by`)
narrow it as they narrow the view. `-o FILE.md` or `-o FILE.json` writes
either to a file.

The snapshot uses `schema_version: 3`. `changes` lists logical changes:
a change Word wrote as several marks is one entry with its `members`,
and a deletion followed by its author's insertion is one `replacement`.
`summary.tables` and `tables[]`
count top-level body tables only; each `index` is the view's `tN`.
Every table has a `nested` array (empty for a leaf), containing its cell tables.
A nested entry has `parent` (for example `t0.row2.cell0`) and no `index`.
A deeper parent includes the cell-local table ordinal, for example
`t0.row2.cell0.t0.row0.cell1`. Paragraph ids and edit-plan schemas are unchanged.

`--tables` numbers only top-level tables as `table N`, matching `tN` in
the view and `-p tN`. Nested tables follow their containing cell row,
indented two spaces per nesting level and labelled `nested in CELL_PATH`.
For example, `nested in t0.row2.cell0`; a further level uses
`t0.row2.cell0.t0.row0.cell1`. `--tables -p t0` includes this whole tree.

```text
<!-- p0 center -->
# Consulting Agreement

<!-- p1 justify -->
This Consulting Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made between Harbor Point Analytics LLC ("Consultant") and Juniper Freight Co. ("Client").

<!-- p2 -->
## 1. Services

<!-- p3 -->
Consultant will deliver the services in each Statement of Work, including {++quarterly++}{r0 @AC} route-cost reports and a {~~weekly~>monthly~~}{r1+2 @AC} review call.
```

Attribution uses braces after the change closer: `{++new++}{r1 @AL}`.
`{>>c5 @AC: note<<}` remains a comment. A deletion inside another author's
insertion names its parent with `{r3 @BO re r1 @AL}`. Distinct revision ids
stay separate; only a deletion directly followed in the rendered stream by
a live insertion from the same author forms `{~~old~>new~~}{r4+5 @AL}`.
Different inline dates keep the two marks separate. An inserted paragraph
mark is `¶{r7 @AL}`. To write literal attribution-shaped text after a closer,
escape the opening brace: `{++new++}\{r1 @AL}`; write literal `¶\{` likewise.

See [docs/MARKDOWN.md](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/MARKDOWN.md#agent-view) for the grammar.

### Validate

```sh
jubarte validate contract.docx
jubarte validate contract.docx --json
jubarte validate contract.docx --repair fixed.docx
jubarte validate review/redline.docx --original contract.docx --author Claude
```

`validate` lists what makes Word refuse or repair a file, beyond what an
XSD sees: one line per finding (`code`, `part#path`, message, a `*` when
it is Word-fatal), or one JSON object each with `--json`. `--repair` writes
a copy with every repairable finding fixed and lists what remains;
`--original` with `--author` audits that every text change against the
original is a revision by that author (`UNTRACKED_EDIT`, `FOREIGN_AUTHOR`),
and that no other author's comment is gone, reworded, resolved or reopened
and every new comment is signed by that author (`FOREIGN_COMMENT`).
The `edits` rules also report permission endpoints lost from any part
(`PERMISSION_RANGE_DROPPED`); losing an editable region is not Word-invalid.
`--rules a11y,style,structure` adds accessibility, style and structure
findings (heading skips, images without alt text, tables without a header
row, literal bullets, stale caches), each located by paragraph id;
`--rules` also takes single rule codes.

`NESTED_SAME_REVISION` is non-fatal: direct same-kind nesting is `info`
(Word opens and reads it faithfully); alternating nesting such as
`ins > del > ins` is a `warning` because Word opens it but misreads
reject-all (#1134, Word probes 2026-10-17).

`NESTED_TEXT_BOX` is a Word-fatal Ring-1 error: a DrawingML or VML text box
inside another box's readable content prevents Word from opening the file
(#1132, Word probes 2026-10-18). The check covers every story part and ignores
nesting only in `mc:Fallback`; `--repair` leaves it unchanged.

Any `word` or `edits` finding exits 2, and so does any `error`; `--strict`
fails on warnings too. A file that cannot be read exits 1.

| Option | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `--json` | JSON Lines: one object per finding, nothing when there is none |
| `--rules SETS` | `word` (the default), `edits`, `a11y`, `style`, `structure`, or rule codes, comma-separated |
| `--strict` | Fail on warnings too |
| `--repair FILE` | Write the repaired package; remaining findings still exit 2 |
| `--original FILE` | Audit tracked edits against this original (needs `--author`) |
| `--author NAME` | The author every change must carry |
| `--force` | Replace an existing `--repair` output |

`jubarte audit FILE` still runs, as `validate --rules a11y,style,structure`
with a note; it is removed in 0.14.

### Scrub

```sh
jubarte scrub contract.docx -o outgoing.docx
jubarte scrub contract.docx -o outgoing.docx --rsids --docprops
```

Removes who touched a document before it goes out: author names (as one
alias, `--author-alias NAME`), rsids, the people and dates in the document
properties, and comments. Text and tracked changes stay. Without a flag all
four go, under the alias "Author"; with flags, only those given.

### Append documents

```sh
jubarte append a.docx b.docx c.docx -o combined.docx
jubarte append a.docx b.docx -o combined.docx --section-break continuous --keep-sections
```

B after A, then C after that, carrying images, links, styles, lists and
notes. Comments are dropped with a warning unless `--carry-comments`.
`--section-break` is `next-page` (the default), `continuous` or `none`;
`--keep-sections` keeps each document's page setup, headers and footers.

### Comments

```sh
jubarte comments contract.docx
jubarte comments contract.docx --json --author "Reviewer" --latest
```

Every comment with its thread (`parent`, `done`) and the text it is
anchored to. Edit plans reply to, resolve, edit and delete comments (see
the operation table below).

### Fields

```sh
jubarte convert contract.docx -o updated.docx --update-fields --report fields.json
```

`--update-fields` refreshes the cached results of `PAGEREF`, `REF`, `NUMPAGES`, `SEQ` and
`TOC` fields from jubarte's layout; TOCs are rebuilt from the headings. Field
codes stay, so Word can update them again. Page numbers are jubarte's layout,
not Word's ([`docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md)). It
runs after `--track-changes accept|reject`; `--report` lists the fields
written with their old and new results.

### Compare rendered pages

```sh
jubarte visual-diff before.docx after.docx
jubarte visual-diff before.docx after.docx --out-dir pages --dpi 150 --json
```

Lays out and rasterizes both documents at one resolution and compares them
pixel for pixel. Exit 0 when every page is the same, 5 when any page
differs; `--out-dir` writes the changed pages, overlays and `diff.json`.

### Apply an edit plan

First read the source:

```sh
jubarte read contract.docx -o contract.json
```

Create `plan.json`:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "source_sha256": "<the sha256: line of jubarte read>",
  "author": "Reviewer",
  "operations": [
    {
      "id": "term",
      "kind": "replace",
      "paragraph": "p12",
      "find": "two years",
      "replacement": "three years"
    }
  ]
}
```

Or record it from flags, one command at a time. Nothing is edited until
the plan runs:

```sh
jubarte edit contract.docx --plan plan.json -p p12 --anchor "two years" --content "three years"
jubarte add contract.docx --plan plan.json -p p14 --comment --content "Why three?"
```

Each recording is checked against `contract.docx` and pins its
`source_sha256`; one that does not apply leaves `plan.json` as it was.
`--consume` deletes the plan once it has been applied.

Preview it:

```sh
jubarte edit contract.docx \
  --plan plan.json \
  --out-dir review \
  --dry-run
```

Apply and render:

```sh
jubarte edit contract.docx \
  --plan plan.json \
  --out-dir review \
  --pdf \
  --png \
  --dpi 100
```

A successful edit can produce:

```text
review/
  clean.docx
  redline.docx
  patch.diff
  report.jsonl
  clean.pdf
  redline.pdf
  clean-page-01.png
  redline-page-01.png
  ...
```

Operation kinds (`jubarte capabilities` lists the ones the installed build
supports):

| Kind | What it does |
|---|---|
| `replace` | Replace `find` with `replacement` in one paragraph; only the words that differ are written, so kept words keep their formatting and characters (a curly quote or a non-breaking space stays where the replacement has the plain one); optional `format` for the new text, `"whole": true` for one deletion then one insertion as typed |
| `insert` | Insert text `after` or `before` a match, or at `position` `start`/`end` |
| `delete` | Delete a match |
| `rewrite` | Give a paragraph's whole new text; only the words that differ are edited |
| `format_run` | Restyle existing text as a tracked formatting change |
| `comment` | Comment on a match, a whole paragraph, or every paragraph up to `through` |
| `reply_comment`, `resolve_comment`, `edit_comment`, `delete_comment` | Work on a comment thread by `comment_id`. Rewording, resolving or deleting another author's comment is allowed and noted; `"others": "keep"` refuses it (`COMMENT_NOT_YOURS`) and a reply is the keeping move. `"rewrite_others_comments": true` is accepted and ignored |
| `strike` | Reject another author's insertion `revision` visibly: your tracked deletion inside it, with an optional `comment` on the struck words |
| `restore` | Reject another author's deletion `revision` visibly: your tracked copy of its words right after it, with an optional `comment` |
| `insert_paragraph` | A new paragraph after the anchor, with its properties (or those `like` selects) |
| `delete_paragraph` | Delete a paragraph, optionally commenting on the deleted text |
| `format_paragraph` | Style, alignment, line spacing, space before and after, as a tracked property change |
| `merge_paragraphs` | Join the next paragraph onto this one |
| `insert_table` | A table before or after a body paragraph, tracked as inserted rows |
| `list` | Bulleted, numbered or lettered list, tracked as property changes |
| `insert_footnote` | A footnote after an anchor |
| `insert_image` | A picture paragraph (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP or TIFF) |
| `insert_toc` | A table of contents field; with `"update_fields": true` it is filled from the headings |
| `page_setup` | Page size, orientation and margins |
| `watermark` | Word's diagonal text watermark in every default header (untracked) |
| `fill_control` | Fill a content control (text, choice, checkbox or date) by id, tag or alias |
| `redact` | Replace text with `█` blocks in both copies, untracked; refused if the text still occurs anywhere. No report, refusal or confirmation repeats the text or the document's copy of it: a plan with a redaction confirms with the published view, not the before/after diff |
| `settings` | `trackRevisions`, `updateFields` and document protection in `word/settings.xml` |

Plans are atomic: stale sources, ambiguous anchors, overlapping edits or
unsupported structures refuse the plan instead of making a guessed edit.

See
[`skills/jubarte-documents/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/skills/jubarte-documents/SKILL.md)
and
[`examples/agents/acme-letter`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/examples/agents/acme-letter)
for the full plan schema and a complete example.

### Capabilities

```sh
jubarte capabilities          # one line per capability
jubarte capabilities --json   # the manifest: formats, ids, validate rules, operation kinds
```

Use this when an application or agent needs to discover the exact surface
supported by the installed build.

### Self-update

```sh
jubarte self-update --check
jubarte self-update
```

Optional:

```text
-y, --yes
--version VERSION
```

See [`docs/SELF_UPDATE.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/SELF_UPDATE.md).

### Debugging DOCX behavior

```sh
jubarte debug FILE.docx --list
jubarte debug FILE.docx --check render
jubarte debug FILE.docx -c text
jubarte debug FILE.docx -c runs
jubarte debug FILE.docx -c xml

jubarte debug diff A.docx B.docx
jubarte debug diff A.docx B.docx C.docx --full
```

`debug` is hidden from `jubarte --help`: it is a diagnostic tool for
engine work, not part of the stable surface. Debug catalogs cover package structure, fields, bookmarks, IDs, styles,
text boxes, revision changes, numbering, normalized XML/text/runs and render
information.

Use `jubarte <command> --help` for the authoritative option list for the
installed release.

## Rendering and fonts

The PDF engine reconstructs Word-oriented layout directly; it does not call
Microsoft Word or LibreOffice.

The documented rendering surface includes:

- tracked changes, and comments as Word's balloons in the markup pane
  (a resolved comment faded, a reply numbered under its thread);
- paragraph/run formatting and advanced line layout;
- CJK and RTL/complex-script text;
- installed and embedded fonts;
- merged, vertically merged, autofit and floating tables;
- DrawingML/VML graphics, text boxes, charts and SmartArt;
- raster and EMF/WMF images;
- headers, footers and floating frames;
- sections, columns, backgrounds and page borders;
- footnotes and selected fields.

Rendering fidelity still depends on fonts and on document features.
WebAssembly has no installed fonts: `docxToPdf` paints with the fonts a
document embeds and the bundled Carlito and Liberation faces, so Chinese,
Japanese or Korean text without an embedded font is not painted (see
[`KNOWN_ISSUES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/KNOWN_ISSUES.md), item 9).

Supplemental font lookup can be configured with:

```sh
export JUBARTE_FONT_DIR=/path/to/jubarte/fonts
export JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX=/path/to/font-index.tsv
```

Set:

```sh
export JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX=off
```

to disable the persistent font index.

Default per-user font directories are documented in the installation section
of this repository.

For known Word-layout differences, see:

- [`docs/WORD_LAYOUT_RULES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/WORD_LAYOUT_RULES.md)
- [`docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md)
- [`docs/WORD_COMMENT_BALLOONS.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/WORD_COMMENT_BALLOONS.md)

## Comparison modes

The default comparison mode is:

```sh
--mode word
```

It targets Word-like comparison behavior.

Classic PowerTools behavior is available with:

```sh
--mode powertools
```

Choose explicitly if exact comparison semantics matter to a regression test
or downstream workflow.

## Existing revisions in edit plans

An edit plan can refuse documents that already contain tracked changes, or
resolve them according to an explicit policy.

List changes before editing:

```sh
jubarte changes source.docx --json
```

Selective resolution can be part of the plan, for example:

```json
{
  "resolve_revisions": {
    "accept": {
      "ids": ["r12"]
    },
    "reject": {
      "authors": ["Previous Reviewer"]
    }
  }
}
```

Conflicting selections are rejected instead of silently choosing a side.

Settling a revision that removes a comment's whole anchor removes the thread
and its replies, as Word does. Edit receipts report each removed thread as
`removed_comments` (using source ids `c0`, `c1`, etc.), each saying `why`:
`anchor removed by accepting r13`, the change that held its mark. Legacy `edit --dry-run`
prints the JSONL preview; `edit --out-dir` writes the summary event in
`report.jsonl`. Typed `edit apply --json` includes the same records in `data`.
To preserve the thread, set `"removed_anchor_comments": "keep"` in a v1 or
v2 plan. Its range markers and reference runs move together to an empty,
untracked anchor where the removed text was. A reply in the same plan can
then use that anchor. The receipt reports `kept_comments` with `anchor: "empty"`.
Comments the plan subsequently deletes are not listed; deleted replies leave
the kept thread's `replies`, while its surviving root stays listed.
This opt-in is a jubarte convention that Word opens with threaded balloons;
the default `"remove"` follows Word's removal behavior. Partial overlaps
keep the existing behavior. Unknown values are refused as `INVALID_PLAN`.
The policy is available in plans; `accept`/`reject` keep their existing warnings.
A reply to a comment whose paragraph the same plan deletes goes on the
deleted text beside its parent, where Word shows the thread; a v2 plan with
`"track": "off"` deletes the anchor outright, and is refused with
`COMMENT_ANCHOR_REMOVED`.
Comment and bookmark ids stay stable while a plan runs, so later operations
still address the source comments. After all operations finish, the preserving
path numbers the revision-free working document once; its clean copy, tracked
replay and operation receipts share that allocation. Pending source revisions
retain their ids. The comparer path retains ids in both outputs: it unions
comments from its original and edited inputs, so numbering only the edited
input would change comment matching. Settlement receipts retain source comment
ids; newly added comments report their written ids.

If settlement removes a kept thread's row, cell or whole table, its empty
anchor moves to the end of the last surviving paragraph before that container
in the same story, or the start of the first paragraph after it. Removed and
kept receipts never list the same comment. Removal text names the acceptance
or rejection that removed the thread; kept text names its published paragraph.

The v1 plan envelope is documented in `schemas/edit-plan-v1.schema.json`,
and the typed v2 schema in `schemas/edit-plan-v2.schema.json`.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
jubarte original.docx revised.docx \
  -o redline.docx \
  --author "Legal"

jubarte changes redline.docx --json

jubarte convert redline.docx \
  -o redline.pdf \
  --revisions word
```

### Python `Document`

```python
import jubarte_redlines as jubarte

doc = jubarte.read("contract.docx")

print(doc.markdown())
snapshot = doc.inspect()
print(snapshot)

pages = doc.to_png(dpi=120)
```

### Agent-style document editing

See
[`examples/agents/acme-letter`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/examples/agents/acme-letter), which includes
an edit plan, generated report and rendered redline page.

## Safety and validation

CI currently includes:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- Clippy with `-D warnings` on the crate and on the Python, WASM
  (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`) and in-process bench bindings
- all-feature Rust tests on Linux, macOS and Windows
- source-based code coverage with a line-coverage floor
- MSRV testing on Rust 1.94 (the all-feature test suite, on Linux)
- `cargo publish --dry-run`
- `cargo-deny`
- REUSE/SPDX checks
- Python binding tests

The project also maintains package/schema validation and real-Microsoft-Word
opening probes for release work because an OOXML document can be schema-valid
and still trigger Word repair behavior.

See:

- [`KNOWN_ISSUES.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/KNOWN_ISSUES.md)
- [`docs/VERSIONING.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/VERSIONING.md)
- [`docs/bench_classes.md`](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/blob/v0.17.0/docs/bench_classes.md)

## Benchmarks

Jubarte maintains Word-oracle benchmarks for both document comparison and
DOCX rendering.

The benchmark methodology, corpus provenance, current numbers and historical
results belong in:

- the [neurotic_docx_bench RESULTS.md](https://github.com/jandira-tech/neurotic_docx_bench/blob/main/RESULTS.md)
- the [page-by-page comparison site](https://jandira-tech.github.io/neurotic_docx_bench/)

Treat these as reproducible project-maintained measurements rather than as a
substitute for testing your own document corpus.

For important production workloads, benchmark representative documents from
your own environment before choosing an engine.

## Supported environments

| Surface | Supported/tested target |
|---|---|
| Rust / CLI | CI tests Linux, macOS and Windows |
| Rust toolchain | Rust 1.94+ |
| Python | CPython 3.10+ |
| Python release wheels | macOS x86_64/arm64, manylinux_2_28 x86_64/arm64, musllinux_1_2 x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64 (abi3, CPython 3.10+) |
| Node | Node 18+ |
| Browser | WebAssembly builds |
| CLI release workflow | Linux x86_64/arm64 (glibc 2.28+, or static musl for Alpine and other musl images), macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64 targets |

Release assets can vary by tag. Check the
[release page](https://github.com/jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines/releases)
before scripting a binary download.

A Word 97-2003 `.doc` converts to `.docx` with the native binary's
`jubarte convert old.doc` (or `jubarte::legacy_doc::doc_to_docx` in Rust):
text, headings, lists, bold, italic and tables. Every other command, and
the Python and JavaScript packages (the npm command line too), refuse a `.doc` (or an encrypted document of any Word
version) with `LEGACY_DOC` and the hint to save it as `.docx` without a
password, and RTF with `UNSUPPORTED_PACKAGE`. Convert them to `.docx` first.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
|---|---|
| PDF layout differs from Word | Verify required fonts; inspect `--font-report`; read `docs/WORD_DIFFERENCES.md` |
| Text is missing or wraps differently | Check font resolution and embedded/system font availability |
| Edit exits with a refusal | Read `report.jsonl` / stdout for `STALE_SOURCE`, `ANCHOR_NOT_FOUND`, `AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR`, `OVERLAPPING_EDITS`, `UNSUPPORTED_STRUCTURE`, etc. |
| `STALE_SOURCE` | Re-run `jubarte read` and regenerate the plan from its new `sha256:` line |
| `AMBIGUOUS_ANCHOR` | Use a paragraph ID or a more specific exact anchor |
| Document already contains revisions | List them with `jubarte changes`; explicitly accept/reject them or set an edit-plan revision policy |
| Comment is present in DOCX but missing from rendered markup | Check the documented comment-balloon limitations and `docs/WORD_COMMENT_BALLOONS.md` |
| Output page count is not exactly Word's | The renderer targets Word behavior but is independent; inspect known differences before treating page count as an invariant |
| Prebuilt archive is absent for a platform | Install with Cargo or build from source; then check the release assets for a later tag |
| Need exact package differences | Use `jubarte debug diff` and the `text`, `runs`, `xml` or `render` debug catalogs |
